```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Download and read the dataset
dataset_url <- "https://minio.la.utexas.edu/compagendas/datasetfiles/US-Public-Gallups_Most_Important_Problem-21.3.csv"
US_opinion <- read.csv(dataset_url)

# 2. Clean and filter the data, saving it into the 'compared_topics' object
compared_topics <- US_opinion %>% 
  filter(majortopic %in% c(1, 16)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(percent))

# 3. Create the ggplot using the newly created dataset name
ggplot(compared_topics, aes(x = year, y = percent, color = as.factor(majortopic))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_discrete(
    labels = c("1" = "Macroeconomics", "16" = "Defense")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "US Public Interest: Macroeconomics & Civil Rights",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Percent",
    color = "Topic"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)

# 1. Directly read your exact data structure safely without any network download issues
raw_text <- "id,year,percent,majortopic,Congress
1,1946,,1,79
2,1947,0.347958,1,80
3,1948,0.221154,1,80
4,1949,0.288126,1,81
5,1950,0.233645,1,81
506,1947,0.00302572,8,80
533,1974,0.100870,8,93
538,1979,0.200403,8,96
1010,1947,0.114977,16,80
1029,1966,0.460043,16,89
1066,2003,0.219876,16,108
1226,1947,0.227685,19,80
1240,1961,0.432272,19,87
1296,2017,0.080921,19,115
1530,2018,0.123755,19,115
1541,2019,0.020493,8,116
1542,2019,0.028239,9,116
1548,2019,0.066346,16,116
1551,2019,0.152802,19,116
1557,2020,0.254421,3,116
1562,2020,0.000428,8,116
1569,2020,0.013119,16,116
1572,2020,0.024574,19,116
1583,2021,0.038666,8,117
1590,2021,0.082395,16,117
1593,2021,0.139873,19,117
1604,2022,0.040260,8,117
1611,2022,0.016258,16,117
1614,2022,0.040158,19,117
1624,2023,0.212249,7,118
1625,2023,0.009074,8,118
1632,2023,0.008488,16,118
1635,2023,0.014922,19,118"

US_opinion <- read.csv(textConnection(raw_text), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# 2. Filter data for the requested topics: Energy (8), Defense (16), and Foreign Policy (19)
compared_topics <- US_opinion %>%
  filter(majortopic %in% c(8, 16, 19)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(percent)) %>%
  mutate(topic_label = case_when(
    majortopic == 8  ~ "Energy Policy",
    majortopic == 16 ~ "Defense & Military",
    majortopic == 19 ~ "Foreign Policy / Int'l Affairs"
  ))

# 3. Dynamic Calculation: Isolate the absolute maximum priority level row for each year
yearly_peaks <- compared_topics %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  filter(percent == max(percent, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# 4. Generate the visualization with custom styling and red stars at the heights
ggplot(compared_topics, aes(x = year, y = percent)) +
  # Transparent filled areas to view structural issue weight overlaps cleanly
  geom_area(aes(fill = topic_label), position = "identity", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(color = topic_label), linewidth = 1.2) +
  
  # The Requested Feature: Red stars (shape 11) matching each year's maximum priority height
  geom_point(data = yearly_peaks, aes(x = year, y = percent), 
             shape = 11, color = "#FF0000", size = 4, stroke = 1.2) +
  
  # Custom aesthetic configurations & distinct thematic color palette
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Energy Policy" = "#E69F00",                  # Gold
    "Defense & Military" = "#009E73",             # Sage Green
    "Foreign Policy / Int'l Affairs" = "#0072B2"  # Blue
  )) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Energy Policy" = "#E69F00",
    "Defense & Military" = "#009E73",
    "Foreign Policy / Int'l Affairs" = "#0072B2"
  )) +
  
  # Typography adjustments
  labs(
    title = "US Priorities: Foreign Policy, Defense, and Energy",
    subtitle = "Red stars indicate the highest priority point among the three categories for each calendar year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Percentage of Public Mentions",
    color = "Agenda Issue",
    fill = "Agenda Issue"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray40"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray92")
  )

```
